SIRD-GA from daily cases and deaths

Source: vignettes/sird-ga-article.Rmd
sird-ga-article.Rmd
library(epicurves)

This vignette shows the functions behind the article on what reported cases and deaths can identify in a stochastic SIRD model (Ospina, Oliveira, Ferraz and Gondim). The heavier computations of the article are shown but not run.

Simulated cases and deaths

sird_ga_simulate_inc() simulates the SIRD jump process exactly and turns its daily increments into reported cases (binomial thinning with probability p plus measurement error with variance tau2 times the latent count) and reported deaths (probability q, variance scale tau2_d).

set.seed(1)
N <- 20000
si <- sird_ga_simulate_inc(N, S0 = N - 10, I0 = 10, R0 = 0, lambda = 0.6, gamma = 0.3,
                           alpha = 0.1, p = 0.5, tau2 = 0.16, q = 1, tau2_d = 0.1, Tmax = 100)
c(cases = sum(si$cases), deaths = sum(si$deaths))
#>  cases deaths 
#>   5826   2988

Fitting to cases and deaths

sird_ga_fit_inc() maximises the Kalman-filter log-likelihood of the Gaussian approximation, with the death reporting probability held at q = 1 (the product of q and the death rate is what the death counts identify).

fit <- sird_ga_fit_inc(si$cases, si$deaths, N, use = "both",
                       starts = list(list(lambda = 0.5, gamma = 0.25, alpha = 0.15, i0 = 5e-4,
                                          p = 0.6, tau2 = 0.3, tau2_d = 0.3)),
                       nsub = 5L)
round(fit$theta[c("lambda", "gamma", "alpha", "p")], 3)
#> lambda  gamma  alpha      p 
#>  0.662  0.323  0.110  0.491
fit$loglik
#> [1] 1536.861

The death rate is not identifiable from cases alone

With cases only, recovery and death enter the likelihood through gamma + alpha. The profile log-likelihood of alpha is flat when fitted to cases and has a maximum when deaths are added:

fit_c <- sird_ga_fit_inc(si$cases, NULL, N, use = "cases",
                         starts = list(list(lambda = 0.5, gamma = 0.25, alpha = 0.15,
                                            i0 = 5e-4, p = 0.6, tau2 = 0.3)),
                         free = c("lambda", "gamma", "alpha", "i0", "p", "tau2"))
grid <- c(0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3)
sird_ga_profile(fit_c, si$cases, NULL, "alpha", grid)
sird_ga_profile(fit, si$cases, si$deaths, "alpha", grid)

Paraíba: weekly data and transmission changing every four weeks

The application aggregates the daily counts of 2020 into complete epidemiological weeks (daily counts carry a strong weekly reporting cycle) and lets the transmission rate change every four weeks with sird_ga_fit_tv(). Rates are then per week.

data(paraiba_covid19)
data(paraiba_population)
d <- paraiba_covid19
wk <- d$epi_week
keep <- wk %in% names(which(table(wk) == 7))
cases <- as.numeric(tapply(d$new_cases[keep], wk[keep], sum))
deaths <- as.numeric(tapply(d$new_deaths[keep], wk[keep], sum))
blk <- ceiling(seq_along(cases) / 4)
c(weeks = length(cases), blocks = max(blk))
#>  weeks blocks 
#>     40     10
rem <- 7 / 7  # removal rate per week for a mean infectious period of 7 days
st <- list(lambda = rep(1.2 * rem, max(blk)), gamma = 0.98 * rem, alpha = 0.02 * rem,
           i0 = 5e-6, p = 0.2, tau2 = 20, tau2_d = 2)
f <- sird_ga_fit_tv(cases, deaths, paraiba_population, blk, "both", st, nsub = 20L)
7 / (f$theta[["gamma"]] + f$theta[["alpha"]])   # mean infectious period, days
tapply(f$R_t, blk, mean)                         # reproduction number by block

The same model can be written with the general engine (vignette("compartmental-models")): ga_model() with infection, recovery and death events, ga_incidence() streams for infection and death, and blocks = list(lambda = blk) in ga_fit().
